Brief facts of the case, as per the prosecution's story, are that the complainant Ammad Shah ASI and Muhammad Aqib C/1513, on 20.04.2022, were patrolling at Tramri Chowk, Lethrar Road in a private vehicle when they received information from a special informer that a drug peddler Adnan son of Zaman was openly selling powder and ice in the street of his house at Mohallah Chaudhrian Tarlai Kalan. On such information they took the officials of Eagle Squad, namely, Muhammad Akmal C/2539, Muhammad Sadiq C/4048, Farakh Rashid C/2426 and Sajid Nawaz C/8931, who were on duty at Lethrar road, with them and they reached Mohallah Chaudhrian near Haveli Syed Gui at about 1:10 AM. Then at the pointation of informer when police party moved forward to control the two-armed accused, who were admonished to disarm themselves, but instead they opened straight fire upon the police party with the intention of murder. One straight fire shot of accused Adnan landed on the chest of Muhammad Aqib C/1513 and he got injured and fell, meanwhile, the two accused took advantage of narrow streets and decamped the place of occurrence. The injured constable succumbed to injuries in a private vehicle on the way to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital ('PIMS'). "6. Both the appellants were jointly seated in the lineup. The· idea of identification parade or lineup is to stand or seat the suspect in a group of ·persons (dummies or fillers) that closely resemble the characteristics of the suspect, in order to test the recognition, memorv. perception and observation of the witness and thus verify the testimony of the witness. Placing two or more suspects jointly in an identificationparade (or joint parade), tarnishes the homogeneity, sameness and identicalness of the members of the parade and defeats the very purpose of having a test identification parade. Joint parade passes for suggestive and indicative identification, compromising the reliability of the witness and opening doors to misidentification,rendering TIP unsafe and untrustworthy. See: In the matter of Kanwar Anwaar Ali (PLJ 2019 SC (Cr.C.) 153) onjoint identificationparade."

TIP proceedings are silent regarding the description of the unknown accused given by ·the complainant in the report. TIP can onlv commence, once suspects matching the description in the crime report or in the statements of the witnesses under section 161 Cr.P.C have been arrested. Matching the description in the first information report is the starting point towards identification of the unknown accused. It is, therefore, uncertain how the appellants were hurled and lined-up for the identification parade without the · Magistrate first matching the description given by the complainant. Selection of the suspects, without any correlation with description of the accused in the first information report, raises doubts and makes the . identification proceedings unsafe and doubtful rendering the identification evidence inconsequential. This is just a shade apart from cases where there is no description ofthe accused in the FIR. the effect being the same, casting doubts on the credibility of the test identification parade. "6. We have given our anxious consideration to the contentions of the learned counsel of the parties and perused the record. It is an admitted fact that the complainant had not mentioned the name of any of the accused in the F.LR. He also did not mention description/features of the accused persons in the F.LR. It is settled principle of law that it is the duty and obligation of the complainant to give material particulars of the case in the contents of the F.LR. without giving detail of incidental matter as per law laid down by this Court in Muhammad Hussain's case (1993 SCMR 1614).... It is also settled principle of law that picking out of accused in identification parade is not a substantive piece of evidence. Such evidence is merely corroborative piece of evidence. The prosecution has attempted to complete the chain of circumstantial evidence by medical evidence relating to the post mortem examinations of the deceased persons. This evidence proves only the factum that death of the deceased persons was caused by cutting their throats through some sharp edge weapon; it does in no way indicate who had cut their throats and with what particular weapon. Medical evidence is in the nature of supporting, confirmatory or explanatory of the direct or circumstantial evidence, and is not "corroborative evidence" in the sense the term is used in legal parlance for a piece of evidence that itself also has some probative force to connect the accused person with the commission· of offence. Medical evidence bv itself does not throw anv light on the identify of the offender. Such evidence may confirm the available substantive evidence with regard to certain facts including seat of the injury. nature of the injury. cause of the death, kind of the weapon used in the occurrence, duration between the injuries and the death, and presence of an injured witness or the injured accused at the place of occurrence, but it does not connect the accused with the commission of the offence. It cannot constitute corroboration for proving involvement of the accused person in the commission of offence, as it does not establish the identify of the accused person.

Therefore, the medical evidence is of little help to the prosecution for bringing home the guilt to the petitioners." State (Supra) eloquently expounded on the nature of medical evidence in the following terms:
